newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: UN official hopeful for Cambodia polls.
newsitem.headline: UN official hopeful for Cambodia polls.

text.p: The United Nations, which organised Cambodia's watershed elections in 1993, believes polls due for next year and 1988 can be held as planned despite some delays, a U.N. official said on Tuesday.
Phnom Penh plans to hold local elections next year and general elections in 1998, five years after the first free and fair elections in more than two decades.

This time the United Nations is only providing advice and technical coordination on elections at the request of co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, U.N. Assistant Secretary General for Political Affairs Alvaro de Soto told reporters.
De Soto, wrapping up six days of discussions with government officials on the polls, said he had found that preparations for elections were always behind schedule.
The official, who met both premiers, King Norodom Sihanouk and parliament chief Chea Sim, added that the United Nations was "neither alarmed nor dismayed by the delay that has occurred so far..."
Analysts say a huge amount still needed to be done, including the introduction of laws governing the electoral process and political parties.
De Soto stressed that his mission in Cambodia was only to give advice.
"No one has asked for a renewal of UNTAC (U.N. Transitional Authority in Cambodia)...There will not be an UNTAC II," he said.

UNTAC supervised the multi-party 1993 elections which saw the royalist FUNCINPEC party emerge with the most seats and form an uneasy coalition with the incumbent former communists of the Cambodian Peoples' Party (CPP).
